page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-4GB is a budget-oriented virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs allocated as shared physical cores with 1 thread per core and 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a 30 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show a strong contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded gzip compression all ranking in the top tier. However, due to the shared CPU allocation and 2-core limit, multi-core metrics like Geekbench multi-core and software compilation fall into the bottom tier. Memory performance is mixed, with average large-block read and write bandwidths but a weak PassMark memory score.

Given its shared CPU allocation and starter hardware profile, this server offers a highly cost-efficient entry point for lightweight workloads that do not require sustained, intensive multi-core processing. It is well-suited for single-threaded tasks, text processing, basic web serving, and lightweight Redis caching. However, it is not recommended for heavy database operations, software compilation, or multi-threaded rendering due to its lower multi-core performance and memory throughput constraints.
